lens_summary: METRIC ANATOMY (tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/metrics.py, verified on synthetic graphs with the official code, scratchpad synth.py/synth2.py): score = sum_i D_i*J_i*(1-0.1*(N_pred_i-N_est_i)/N_est_i)/sum_i D_i + 0.1*divJ_micro, with D_i = TP_i+FP_i+FN_i (NOT the GT edge count as BRIEF says). The multiplier is linear with no kink and no cap above 1 (N_est=2*N_pred gives adj 1.05); only max(0,.) clips. N_est comes from GT metadata and is unknown at test time, but it does not matter for decisions: every node costs exactly 0.1*J_i/N_est_i whether we are above or below N_est. In TP-edge units a node costs 1/1397 of a TP edge on 44b6-type videos and 1/204 on 6bba-type videos (D and N_est per video from research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_metric.notes.md). Unannotated tracks and forks are free; an isolated duplicate 0.5 um from a GT node steals the match and turns 2 TP into 2 FN + 2 FP; a swap (GT nucleus between two of our tracks, closest-track order flips once) costs 1 FN + 2 FP, i.e. 3 error units; a fork on an annotated non-dividing cell costs 1 edge FP + 1 division FP; a fork 1 frame late is still a division TP. PUBLIC DECOMPOSITION: 0.950 = adj ~0.914 + 0.1*0.36 (J_div from probe 26: 0.947 -> 0.911 with zero forks, experiments/RESULTS.md:59). Reaching 0.96/0.97/0.975/0.99 needs +0.010/+0.020/+0.025/+0.040. By one term alone: division J 0.46/0.56/0.61/0.76; or adjusted edge 0.924/0.934/0.939/0.954, i.e. 12/23/29/47% fewer edge errors; or 11/22/27/44% fewer nodes with zero TP loss (scratchpad arith.py). 0.99 is not reachable legitimately by 29 Sep. It needs roughly half of all edge errors removed, or a mix such as adj 0.934 + J_div 0.56. That is beyond the 0.969-0.975 top teams, who retrained models over weeks. The only metric route to ~0.99 would be the multiplier: deleting nearly every unannotated node gives x1.09, so 0.914*1.09 ~ 0.997. That needs knowledge of which cells are annotated, which only the test labels give, so it is excluded. DIVISIONS are the most leveraged events on the public board. J=0.36 forces public fork precision >= 0.40 (recall <= 0.8), versus 0.35 in the in-sample lab. One extra division TP is worth +0.0010..+0.0040 of score and one removed FP fork +0.0004..+0.0015, depending on the unknown public GT division count G = 20-60. That is 40-150x a TP edge, and it matches the LB noise of ~0.003. The break-even precision for adding a fork is J/(1+J): 0.265 on public, ~0.106 if the private embryo is lab-like (J 0.12). So insertions with marginal precision >= 0.3 and FP removals at ~0 TP are positive under BOTH scenarios. Ceiling of the division term on public: precision 0.6 and recall 0.8 give J 0.52, +0.016. WHY NODE DELETION DID NOT TRANSFER: the bonus per deleted node is fixed and tiny, and the loss is ~1-2 TP edges per deleted annotated node. Break-even needs < ~0.07% (44b6) / ~0.5% (6bba) of the deleted nodes to be annotated. In-sample, the public detector and edge net were trained on those very annotations, so annotated cells get long clean tracks. Short fragments are then depleted of annotated nodes (0.9% vs 3.2% overall, research/wf_ideas/hyp_nodes-metric.notes.md), and a junkier pipeline sees a large 'free' bonus offline. On test, annotated tracks are the difficult ones (hengck23, research/discussions_summary.md) and fragment out of sample, so deletion hits them. LB evidence: min track len 6->4 -0.002 and 6->8 -0.001 (CONTEXT.md:170,180), det 0.99 -0.005, Justin CH123's losses tracked node drops, B25 pruning negative even in the lab. The asymmetric corollary: node ADDITIONS are nearly free on the multiplier. They lose only through match-stealing and wrong links, which the in-sample lab cannot measure (annotated recall 0.983). The recall side is therefore the direction the metric favours, but it is unvalidatable offline. HONEST CEILING OF THIS LENS: no hidden legitimate lever with ceiling >= +0.01 exists outside (a) the division term and (b) localisation/recall, which is detector work. The four ideas below are metric-grounded; each has a ceiling of +0.004 to +0.016 but an expected public gain of only +0.001 to +0.003. The realistic end state remains ~0.955-0.960 public, in line with the v2 synthesis, with the division term the only place where a +0.01 step is arithmetically possible.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: BRIEF: adjusted edge is weighted by GT edge count per video.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The official summarise() weights by w_i = TP_i+FP_i+FN_i, so a video's weight grows with its own FP. Harmless for ranking, but lab re-implementations should use D_i.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/metrics.py summarise(): weights = edge_tp+edge_fp+edge_fn; tools/official/metrics.md 'w_i = TP_i + FP_i + FN_i'.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Predicting fewer nodes than N_est is a special bonus region / matching N_est is a target.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The multiplier is linear in N_pred with no kink and no cap above 1, so the marginal value of a node is 0.1*J_i/N_est_i everywhere. N_est is irrelevant to any decision.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: metrics.py per_sample_metrics; synthetic check: N_est=2*N_pred -> adj 1.05, 0.5*N_pred -> 0.90 (scratchpad synth.py).

challenged_assumptions.assumption: The x138 head's gain on our base (+0.002) is localisation, reduced because our post-ILP stages do not consume positions.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The head drops final nodes by 2.9% on the dummy clips (10.7% on 44b6_0b24845f). At pure-bonus value that is 0.1*0.029*0.91 = +0.0026, the whole exp51-exp48 gain. On our base the localisation share may be ~0. On x138, readmit re-adds ILP-dropped peaks next to open track ends ('drop then readmit'). That also means the head's private gain depends on how many nodes it drops on the private embryo.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md section 4 (122,704 -> 119,174 nodes); CONTEXT.md 2026-09-25 00:39 (exp51 0.950 vs exp48 0.948); x138 readmit code in experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/exp56-x138-verbatim.ipynb (readmit_discarded_detections).

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Min-track-length / node pruning should give the adjusted-Jaccard bonus (+0.012 for -13% nodes).
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The bonus is real, but the loss side is measured in-sample, where annotated cells almost never fragment. On test, annotated 'difficult' tracks fragment. Break-even needs < 0.07-0.5% annotated among deleted nodes, while even in-sample short fragments are 0.9% annotated.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: research/wf_ideas/hyp_nodes-metric.notes.md; CONTEXT.md:170,180 (min len 4/8 both negative on LB); experiments/RESULTS.md:100 (B25 negative at every fraction); research/discussions_summary.md (Justin CH123, hengck23).

challenged_assumptions.assumption: v2: the lab's division numbers (J 0.12, p 0.35) calibrate division decisions.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Public J 0.36 is impossible at precision 0.35: it needs p >= 0.40 for any recall <= 0.8. The public embryo is division-easy and the break-evens differ (0.265 vs 0.106). A change is safe only if it is positive under both, e.g. insertions with marginal precision >= 0.3 and FP removals at ~0 TP.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: v2: ceiling ~0.962, 0.965+ arithmetically impossible by post-processing.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Mostly right for edges. But the division term alone has +0.016 of public headroom at p 0.6 / r 0.8, and the per-event value is so high that 4-5 extra public division TP is +0.01. It is unlikely (recall is bounded by detection and the orphan rule), not arithmetically impossible.

hypotheses.title: Division budget on x138 set at the public break-even: DaughterNet insertion ladder, positive under both public and lab-like J
hypotheses.mechanism: Division events carry 40-150x the value of an edge TP on the public board: +0.0010..+0.0040 per TP, +0.0004..+0.0015 per removed FP fork for G = 20-60 public GT divisions. Public J 0.36 implies precision >= 0.40, while the break-even precision for an added fork is J/(1+J) = 0.265 (0.106 if private is lab-like). Our fork budget was tuned in the lab at J 0.12, where insertion looks better and removal worse than on public. x138 ships with no insertion (safe-div + DeepCenter 0.25 only). The lab measured added-fork precision 4/15 = 27% (v1, steal), right at the public break-even. So the marginal forks must come from the upper part of the DaughterNet ranking, not from a bigger cap.
hypotheses.change: On the x138 base (tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 --patch divinsert): read #34/#35 first. If #35 >= #34, one probe with a TIGHTER high-precision insertion (DIVINS threshold 0.4 -> 0.6, cap 4 -> 2 per video, steal on). If #35 > #34 + 0.002, one probe with a LOOSER insertion (threshold 0.3, cap 6). Nodes and coordinates stay identical; only forks change.

evidence.claim: Added-fork precision 4/15 with DaughterNet v1 steal; lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001
Beyond cap 4 the marginal is 0 TP / +2 FP in the lab
x138 + insertion adds 12 forks on the 4 dummy clips

hypotheses.upper_bound: Division term headroom on public: 0.1*(1-0.36) = +0.064. Realistic ceiling at p 0.6 / r 0.8: J 0.52 -> +0.016 (arith.py). Insertion alone is bounded by the orphan/steal pool, 97/151 = 64% reach with steal in the lab (b32 audit). Ceiling of this change ~+0.006 (guess: +2-4 public TP at the high-G/low-G per-TP values).
hypotheses.expected_private_gain: +0.000..+0.002 (private per-TP value smaller because D_div is larger on 71% of the test; break-even 0.106 makes insertion safer if private is lab-like)
hypotheses.probability: 0.35 that the better of the two ladder points beats #35 by >= +0.002. The #28 precedent (+0.001) and LB noise 0.003 (~1 division TP) keep it low.
hypotheses.validation_protocol: Pre-registered before any LB slot, on the lab replay with DaughterNet OOF-by-embryo p: (1) marginal forks of each ladder point vs its neighbour must have evaluable precision >= 0.30 on 199 videos AND on each embryo separately, with dTP >= +2; (2) nodes and edges not touched by forks byte-identical. LB adoption: >= #35 + 0.003 (above the noise quantum). Else keep #35, never pick a near-copy by max public score (winner's curse).

hypotheses.title: Second-daughter recovery from x138's in-kernel sub-threshold peak dump (no second GPU pass)
hypotheses.mechanism: In the lab, ~27% of missed GT divisions have the second daughter missing: 23 with no node and 12 claimed by unscored relink, of 132 FN. A 0.90 full-frame pass reached 151/151 GT divisions (B35 step A). It was rejected only because it needed a second detector pass and +24% candidate NODES. x138 already dumps every peak >= 0.3 per frame (BIOHUB_LOWDET_THRESHOLD 0.3) for readmit/gapfill, so the candidate daughters exist in the kernel for free. On the metric side, the added node costs 1/204-1/1397 of a TP edge; one public division TP is worth +0.001..+0.004; one FP fork costs 0.0004..0.0015 plus one edge FP. Forks on unannotated cells are free.
hypotheses.change: New post-linefit patch on x138: for single-child parents ranked by DaughterNet p (top of ranking, cap 2-4 per video), take the best free low-det peak at t+1 (>2 um from any node) at sister geometry. Geometry: 5-14 um from the existing child, <= 9 um from the parent, on the far side of the parent (mirror gate from base rates: step median 5.7 um, sister median 8.85 um). Add it as a node with the fork edge. Optionally extend it one frame with the next low-det peak within 5 um so the branch has a grandchild. Never touch existing nodes or edges.

hypotheses.validation_protocol: Lab: the exp39 replay plus friend A's B35 0.90 peak cache (tools/recover_daughters.py output) as the stand-in for the dump. DaughterNet p OOF by embryo. Pre-registered gate: added forks' evaluable precision >= 0.30 on each embryo, dTP >= +3 on 199, edge TP loss <= 5. The detector is in-sample, so peaks on annotated daughters are optimistic; require the gate at dump threshold 0.9 AND 0.5. LB: adopt only if >= base + 0.003.

hypotheses.title: Recall-side node budget on x138: lower READMIT_MIN_SCORE and widen the gap-filler budget (env knobs only)
hypotheses.mechanism: The metric prices a node at 1/204 (6bba-type) to 1/1397 (44b6-type) of a TP edge. The out-of-sample failure mode is fragmentation of annotated 'difficult' tracks, the same mechanism that made node deletion fail on the LB (min len 4/8 both negative, det 0.99 -0.005). x138's readmit re-adds only peaks >= 0.965 within 4 um of an open end or start. Readmitted peaks that do not link stay isolated and the prune removes them, so failed additions cost nothing. The x138 kernel already has the >= 0.3 peak dump, so sub-threshold continuations of broken tracks are one knob away. The in-sample lab cannot value this (annotated recall 0.983), so the LB is the only test.

hypotheses.title: Sign-robust division FP removal on x138 safe-division forks (midpoint >= 4.5 um), positive under every J scenario
hypotheses.mechanism: An FP fork costs 0.1*J/D_div: +0.0004..+0.0015 per removed FP on public, where D_div is small and each event is worth a lot. Removing a fork at ~0 TP is positive under public J 0.36 and lab-like J 0.12. In the lab, TP forks have a parent-to-daughter-midpoint distance <= 3.8 um, while mid >= 4.0 removed 11 FP / 0 TP (25% of 43 FP). x138's safe-division stage uses DeepCenter 0.25 and none of our fork hygiene. It can ride in the same kernel as the div ladder, since both only edit forks.
